identity.name: Kingdom of Burma (Konbaung dynasty)
native_names: ကုန်းဘောင် (Konbaung)

land.text: the Konbaung realm of Bodawpaya (reigned 1782-1819), which Cliopatria carries on unchanged as 'Burma' from 1820

predecessors.note: The same state: the Konbaung page dates the dynasty from 29 February 1752 to 29 November 1885. Cliopatria changes Name in 1820; the Konbaung Dynasty dossier (another group) should end in 1819 and hand over here, or the two be merged.

successors.note: Lower Burma, Arakan and Tenasserim had passed to the British in 1826 and 1853; the Shan states 'became independent until the British incorporation' (Third Anglo-Burmese War page).

keyframe_review.note: 698,259 km2 against the infobox's 794,000 km2 for 1824 (ratio 0.88). Cliopatria's 1820-1821 shape continues the Konbaung Dynasty shape of 1819 (2,334 cells against 2,413) and lacks Assam, Nagaland and Arunachal, which the 1822 shape adds (372 cells); the page says Assam was under Burmese control from 1817. The corrected shape is the 1822 shape for 1820-1821. Cliopatria draws the Shan states, the Kachin hills and (to 1825) Manipur as direct land; the Konbaung page says the Shan states 'were never directly controlled by the Burmese' and that the Kachin, Palaung and Manipuri principalities were tributary fiefdoms, autonomous in practice, so they are taken out and tinted as vassals by the ledger.

region.text: Burma in 1820 with Assam, Arakan and Tenasserim, without the tributaries

ledger.note: 1820: Cliopatria's 'Burma' row begins, the Konbaung kingdom of Bodawpaya's successor. The dynasty was established 29 February 1752; Arakan (1784/1785), Manipur (1814) and Assam (1817) were already Burmese (Assam ... was under Burmese control from 1817). The page gives the dates, not boundaries: the core is the 1822 outline without the tributary Shan, Kachin and Manipuri lands.

1820: the Shan states are tributaries of the Burmese crown: Shan states paid tribute at various times, but unlike the Mon lands, they were never directly controlled by the Burmese. The page gives no start date; the relation is carried from the state's first year to the fall of Mandalay.
1820: the Kachin hills are tributary fiefdoms: The Kachin, Palaung and Manipuri principalities were tributary fiefdoms, autonomous in practice. The page gives no start date.
1820: Manipur is a tributary fiefdom (the Kachin, Palaung and Manipuri principalities were tributary fiefdoms); Bodawpaya acquired Arakan, Manipur and Assam (Manipur dated 1814 on the page).
1821: the capital moves from Amarapura to Ava (Inwa), capital Ava, 1765-1783 and 1821-1842.

region.text: Rangoon and its delta, held by the British

ledger.note: 1824: the British enter Rangoon. 'On 11 May 1824, a British naval force entered Rangoon's harbour and found the city empty, since the Burmese had adopted a scorched-earth policy'; they fought around the city until December 1824. The war 'formally broke out on 5 March 1824, following border clashes in Arakan'. The occupier is the British Empire.

region.text: Assam, from which the Burmese were expelled

ledger.note: 1825: Assam is lost: the Burmese were expelled from Assam in the summer of 1825; the Treaty of Yandabo confirmed the cession.
1825: the British invade Arakan. The British invasion began on 1 February 1825.
1825: Arakan is lost. Mrauk-U fell on 1 April 1825, and the Burmese forces withdrew from Arakan.
1825: Arakan passes to the British: Mrauk-U fell on 1 April 1825 and the cession was confirmed at Yandabo (Burma ceded Assam, Arakan, and the Tenasserim coast).

region.text: the Tenasserim coast south of the Salween

ledger.note: 1826: the Treaty of Yandabo is signed on 24 February 1826. Burma ceded Assam, Arakan, and the Tenasserim coast south of the Salween River and agreed to pay an indemnity of one million pounds; Burma also stopped interfering in Cachar and Jaintia.
1826: the war ends on 24 February 1826 with the treaty; the page does not say when the British left Rangoon, so the occupation is ended with the war.

1826: Manipur leaves Burmese suzerainty. The page is inconsistent: the lead says the British gained 'total control' of Manipur and the treaty terms list it among the lands Burma ceded, while the infobox says Manipur 'gains independence'. Cliopatria drops Manipur from the Burma shape in 1825.
1842: the capital moves back from Ava to Amarapura (Amarapura, 1783-1821 and 1842-1857).

region.text: Lower Burma: Pegu, the Irrawaddy delta and Rangoon, 'the province of Pegu would henceforth form part of the Company dominions'

ledger.note: 1852: the Second Anglo-Burmese War. The first substantial blow ... was struck by the Company on 5 April 1852, when Martaban was taken; Rangoon was occupied on 12 April, Bassein seized on 19 May, Pegu taken on 3 June and Prome occupied on 9 October 1852.

region.text: Lower Burma: Pegu, the Irrawaddy delta and Rangoon, 'the province of Pegu would henceforth form part of the Company dominions'

ledger.note: 1853: the war ends 'without any treaty being signed', with the proclamation of annexation of 20 January 1853.

region.text: Lower Burma: Pegu, the Irrawaddy delta and Rangoon, 'the province of Pegu would henceforth form part of the Company dominions'

ledger.note: 1853: Lower Burma is annexed by the British. 'The proclamation of annexation was issued on 20 January 1853'; 'the province of Pegu would henceforth form part of the Company dominions'. The page does not give the new frontier; the region is the cells that leave the Cliopatria shape in 1853.
1857: Mindon's capital moves to Mandalay (Mandalay, 1857-1885).
1875: Mindon cedes the Karenni States. Mindon avoided annexation in 1875 by ceding the Karenni States. The page does not say to whom; Cliopatria keeps 9 Kayah cells in the shape to 1884.

region.text: Upper Burma, the Irrawaddy valley to Mandalay

ledger.note: 1885: the Third Anglo-Burmese War opens on 7 November 1885 ('7-29 November 1885, with sporadic resistance continuing into 1887'), the British acting because they were 'alarmed by the consolidation of French Indochina' (Konbaung page).
1885: Mandalay falls on 28 November and King Thibaw is taken prisoner; the king ordered his troops to lay down their arms.

minus.text: the Shan states and the Kachin hills, tributaries 'never directly controlled by the Burmese'

ledger.note: 1885: Upper Burma passes to British India. The war 'saw the loss of sovereignty of an independent Burma under the Konbaung dynasty'; 'Burma was annexed by the British on January 1, 1886'. The Konbaung page dates the annexation to 29 November 1885.
1885: the Shan states leave Burmese suzerainty: the infobox says the 'Shan States became independent until the British incorporation into British India'.

1885: the Kachin principalities leave the Burmese crown with the kingdom's fall; the page says only that 'the British also extended their control into the tribal areas of the Kachin Hills and Chin Hills', without a date.
1885: the Konbaung kingdom ends: 'Following the war, Burma came under the rule of the British Raj as one of its provinces'; annexation proclaimed on 1 January 1886.

wars.name: First Anglo-Burmese War
wars.outcome: British victory: Treaty of Yandabo, 24 February 1826; Burma cedes Assam, Arakan and the Tenasserim coast, stops interfering in Cachar and Jaintia, pays one million pounds; Manipur independent (or British, the page conflicts).
wars.note: Declared 5 March 1824; Rangoon taken 11 May 1824; Mrauk-U fell 1 April 1825; Burmese expelled from Assam in summer 1825.

wars.name: Second Anglo-Burmese War

zones.text: Lower Burma: Pegu, the Irrawaddy delta and Rangoon, 'the province of Pegu would henceforth form part of the Company dominions'

wars.outcome: British victory without a treaty: Pegu (Lower Burma) annexed by proclamation on 20 January 1853; Pagan Min deposed by Mindon.

wars.name: Third Anglo-Burmese War
wars.outcome: British victory in 7-29 November 1885: Mandalay falls on 28 November, Thibaw taken prisoner; Burma annexed to British India on 1 January 1886.

certainty.note: Hill, Shan and Kachin frontiers are tributary and approximate; the cessions of Arakan and Tenasserim (Yandabo, 24 February 1826) and of Pegu (proclaimed 20 January 1853) are sharp as acts but no page opened gives the boundary line.

notes: SPLIT of the Cliopatria Name 'Burma' (1820..1989) into two states: this dossier takes the 1820-1884 shapes (the Konbaung kingdom, 8 shapes, plus a new 1885 keyframe); the 1948-1989 shapes and the Union of Myanmar row (Q836) are the Union of Burma, dossier union-of-burma. The 1820 row is the Konbaung Dynasty row (1741-1819) continued under another Name: the 1819 and 1820 outlines differ by 79 cells. The Cliopatria Wikidata id Q836 is the modern country (Myanmar), so it is kept on union-of-burma and left null here. Cliopatria errors found: (1) Shan states, Kachin hills and Manipur drawn as direct territory although the Konbaung page calls them tributaries (all keyframes adjusted, vassal events added); (2) Assam is missing from the 1820-1821 shape although Burmese from 1817; (3) Tenasserim is lost in 1825 in Cliopatria but only by the treaty of 24 February 1826 on the page; (4) the Burma row ends in 1884 but the kingdom falls in November 1885; (5) the Karenni cession of 1875 is not drawn. Page silent or in conflict: the Konbaung page gives no reign dates for Bagyidaw, Tharrawaddy (seized the throne 1837) or Pagan's end, so no ruler strip is given; the Konbaung page says The two states fought until 1855, after which Tenasserim went to Burma and Lan Na to Siam, which contradicts the 1826 cession and is not used; Manipur is both ceded and independent on the First Anglo-Burmese War page; the Konbaung page gives 1784 and 1785 for Arakan; the proclamation of annexation of Pegu is 20 January 1853 on the Second Anglo-Burmese War page; Cachar and Jaintia (British protectorates from 1822) are not in a gazetteer; the Chin hills, the Panthay and Siam's Chiang Mai, Kengtung and Chiang Saen are not covered. Counterparts needing dossiers: the Shan principalities (Saopha states) of 1819-1959 (the shan-states dossier covers only the Cliopatria row 1287-1563), Manipur kingdom (to 1826), Kachin principalities, the Karenni States, Cachar and Jaintia. Budget: 4 pages for the kingdom (Konbaung, three Anglo-Burmese wars) plus 2 for the Union of Burma, 6 against 5. Quote policy: single quotation marks enclose only wording that the WebFetch result itself gave in quotation marks; every other statement attributed to a page is a close paraphrase.
